# vendor/rustls-rustcrypto — patched rustls-rustcrypto 0.0.2-alpha

This directory is the upstream **`rustls-rustcrypto` 0.0.2-alpha** (copied verbatim
from crates.io) plus one patch: the `rustls-webpki` dependency is gone. Unlike
`vendor/rustls`, `vendor/h2` and `vendor/hyper`, this crate is a **workspace
member**, wired as a path dependency — not an `exclude`d crate behind
`[patch.crates-io]`. Why is under "What a member buys" below.

## Why vendor a crypto provider

* The provider used `rustls-webpki 0.102.8` — a version inside
  [RUSTSEC-2026-0104] (`< 0.103.13`: reachable panic while parsing a CRL) — for
  exactly one item: `webpki::alg_id`, the table of OID constants the
  `SignatureVerificationAlgorithm` impls report
  (`src/verify/{ecdsa,eddsa,rsa}.rs`). A second copy of webpki in the tree, on a
  version carrying an advisory, to obtain ~20 constants. `rustls-pki-types`
  (already a dependency) re-exports the same table as `pki_types::alg_id`.
* Patching a crates-io dependency requires a path or git source — there is no
  "patch it in place" — so vendoring *is* the mechanism. The patch itself is
  three import lines.
* Precedent for the same swap: `cool-japan/oxitls` publishes
  `oxitls-rustcrypto-provider` 0.3.0, which is this change applied to this same
  0.0.2-alpha source — `lib.rs`, `kx.rs`, `aead/*`, `hash.rs`, `hmac.rs`,
  `sign/*` and `verify.rs` there are byte-identical to 0.0.2-alpha, and the
  differences are the OID import (three files), one `misc.rs` turbofish, one
  `sign.rs` comment and 476 lines of QUIC header protection that upstream 0.0.2
  leaves as `#[allow(dead_code)] // TODO`. Adopting that crate would put crypto
  code published by a three-star personal account in the shipping path; the same
  change belongs in this repository, against the RustCrypto org's source.

## What a member buys (and what the alternative costs)

A path crate that is only patched in is an ordinary dependency: its
dev-dependencies are not resolved — `env_logger`, `hex`, `rcgen` and `bencher`
are dev-dependencies of `vendor/rustls` and are absent from `Cargo.lock` today —
and neither its tests nor clippy run under `cargo test --workspace` /
`cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets`. That is fine for `rustls`, `h2` and
`hyper`, whose behaviour our own tests pin. It is not fine for the provider that
performs certificate signature verification: the vendored copy would be the one
piece of the crypto path with no automated coverage at all, which is the opposite
of why one vendors. As a member it is built, linted and tested against the
patched `rustls` in exactly the configuration that ships. The cost is its five
test files (239 lines, upstream's builder tests) joining `cargo test --workspace`.

## What the patch changes

`PATCH.diff` — 155 lines across seven files, against pristine 0.0.2-alpha:

| File | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `src/verify/ecdsa.rs` | `use webpki::alg_id;` folded into the existing `use pki_types::{…}` |
| `src/verify/eddsa.rs` | same |
| `src/verify/rsa.rs` | same |
| `src/kx.rs` | the X25519 group rejects a non-contributory (low-order) peer key with `InvalidKeyShare` — the one *semantic* change in this patch, see below |
| `src/misc.rs` | the `transmute` in `const_concat_slices!` gets its type arguments: clippy 1.98 reports `missing_transmute_annotations` (a warning, and this workspace lints with `-D warnings`) |
| `src/lib.rs` | drop `clippy::from_iter_instead_of_collect` from the crate's own `#![warn(…)]` — the lint was removed from clippy, so naming it is itself a warning |
| `Cargo.toml` | drop `[dependencies.webpki]`, `webpki/alloc`, `webpki/std`; drop the `getrandom 0.2` dev-dependency (it existed for the `validation/` crates that are not shipped) and `resolver = "1"` (a hack for that dev-dependency, ignored for a member); replace cargo's autogenerated header, which pointed at a `Cargo.toml.orig` this tree does not carry |

`src/kx.rs` is the only edit here that changes behaviour on the wire-adjacent path,
and it is deliberate. RFC 8446 §4.2.8.2 requires aborting when the X25519 shared
secret is the identity: a peer key of low order makes it all zeros, i.e. a secret
the peer knows. `x25519-dalek` computes that happily and only *reports* it through
`was_contributory()`, and upstream reads the report nowhere — not in 0.0.2-alpha,
not in `master` — while the `ring` and `aws-lc-rs` providers reject the share. So a
server offering a low-order share used to complete a handshake here on a
predictable secret. `crates/dpi-core/src/net/pq_kx.rs` had inherited the same
omission for its two X25519 paths (the hybrid one is pure X25519) and carries the
check as well. Both are covered by tests:
`net::tls::tests::provider_x25519_group_rejects_a_low_order_peer_key` and
`net::pq_kx::tests::rejects_a_low_order_x25519_share`.

The `misc.rs` and `lib.rs` rows are the price of being a member rather than a
patched-in dependency: the crate is linted by CI, so it has to satisfy the same
clippy the rest of the workspace does. Both edits are in `oxitls`'s fork as well —
the `misc.rs` annotation is one of the four changes it carries beyond the `webpki`
swap.

## What is deliberately *not* patched

* **QUIC header protection** (the 476 lines `oxitls` added). Every suite here is
  declared `quic: None` and nothing in this workspace speaks QUIC; if a UDP/443
  probe ever lands, that is where to start, but it is not this patch.
* **The post-quantum group.** Upstream `master` still ships
  `ALL_KX_GROUPS = [X25519, SecP256R1, SecP384R1]` with no ML-KEM anywhere
  (`grep -r ml-kem src/` → nothing), so ours stays in
  `crates/dpi-core/src/net/pq_kx.rs` and is offered through
  `net::tls::crypto_provider_with_pq`. Keeping it out of this crate is what lets
  the patch stay a dependency edit plus one check.
* **Trimming what we do not use** (`quic.rs`, `sign/*`, the `KeyProvider`). The
  client path here loads no client certificate, but the saving has to be
  measured (`cargo bloat`, `--release` diff) before it is worth editing crypto
  code this repository does not own.

## Files dropped from the crate

`CHANGELOG.md`, `Cargo.toml.orig`, `.cargo-ok`, `.cargo_vcs_info.json`,
`.github/`, `.gitignore` — registry and CI metadata. `examples-external/`,
`tests-external/` and `validation/` — manifest-less harnesses for the author's
own targets (badssl, `no_std` consumers) with dependency requirements this
workspace does not share.

## Rebasing

### Onto another 0.0.2-alpha-era source

```bash
rm -rf vendor/rustls-rustcrypto
cp -r <upstream-rustls-rustcrypto-<version>> vendor/rustls-rustcrypto
rm -f  vendor/rustls-rustcrypto/{Cargo.toml.orig,.cargo-ok,.cargo_vcs_info.json,CHANGELOG.md,.gitignore}
rm -rf vendor/rustls-rustcrypto/{.github,examples-external,tests-external,validation}
patch -p1 -d vendor/rustls-rustcrypto -i vendor/rustls-rustcrypto/PATCH.diff
```

Expect hunks only in the seven files above. Conflicts in the three `verify/*.rs`
imports or in `src/kx.rs` mean upstream touched the same lines, and that is exactly
where the patch has to be re-applied by hand — the `was_contributory()` check in
particular is a change upstream has so far declined to make (it is absent from
both 0.0.2-alpha and `master`), so expect it to conflict on every rebase.

### Onto the next RustCrypto generation (not a re-apply — a port)

Measured 2026-09-18: `master` is mid-migration from the generation this tree uses
(`aes-gcm 0.10`, `sha2 0.10`, `p256 0.13`, `x25519-dalek 2`, `rsa 0.9`) to the
next one (`aead 0.6`, `aes-gcm 0.11`, `sha2 0.11`, `p256/p384 0.14`,
`x25519-dalek 3`, `ed25519-dalek 3`, `rsa 0.10.0-rc.18`, `getrandom 0.4`), and
the released version is still 0.0.2-alpha. Between 0.0.2-alpha and `master` the
*only* semantic differences are that migration plus this same `webpki` removal —
the algorithms, suites, groups and code structure are otherwise the same (largest
per-file diffs: `sign/ecdsa.rs` 15 lines, `aead/gcm.rs` 11, `quic.rs` 11). Before
rebasing onto a release of the new generation, answer the duplicate-crate
question: `pq_kx.rs` pins `x25519-dalek 2` and `ml-kem 0.3`, so the new
generation would put two dalek majors in the tree, and `rsa 0.10.0-rc` would
place a release candidate in the certificate-verification path. Staying on this
base costs nothing today; the alpha dependency label is gone either way, because
the source is now ours.

## Verification

* `cargo tree -i rustls-webpki` → exactly one entry, `0.103.x` (the `rustls`
  one). That is the entire point of the patch.
* `cargo test -p rustls-rustcrypto` — upstream's builder tests, which now run as
  part of `cargo test --workspace` because the crate is a member: the provider
  builds client and server configs and is not FIPS.
* `cargo test -p dpi-core net::` — our tests in `crates/dpi-core/src/net`:
  * `tls::tests::provider_reports_the_algorithm_identifiers_a_certificate_carries`
    pins the OIDs the provider presents as hardcoded DER constants, so a wrong
    import cannot pass;
  * `tls::tests::verifying_handshake_accepts_the_fixture_chain` runs a real
    verifying handshake against a local rustls server with a fixture CA (ECDSA
    P-256, RSA and Ed25519 leaves), and
    `verifying_handshake_rejects_a_chain_whose_ca_is_not_trusted` is its control:
    the same server with an empty root store must be rejected, otherwise a client
    that accepted anything would pass both. Signature verification is the only
    thing the `webpki` swap can break, and it is reached only when the
    certificate is verified — the probes' `TlsProfile::insecure` configurations
    never verify anything, so no JA3/JA4 test covers it;
  * `tls::tests::provider_x25519_group_rejects_a_low_order_peer_key` and
    `pq_kx::tests::rejects_a_low_order_x25519_share` cover the `src/kx.rs` check
    and its two counterparts in our own group (whose `complete_hybrid_component`
    path is pure X25519).
* There is no upstream conformance suite to borrow. `rustls/rustls` does carry
  `rustls-provider-test`, but it is `publish = false`, pins `rustls` to the
  path of `0.24.0-dev.1` in its own tree and depends on `rustls-aws-lc-rs`, so it
  cannot be pointed at a 0.23 provider without forking and porting it. `cargo
  deny` would only be worth adding for advisories we no longer have.
* Manual, with a real network: a run of test 1, whose DoT/DoH probes verify
  against the real roots.

[RUSTSEC-2026-0104]: https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0104.html
